conviction_note: The leasing half is pre-released (Q2 update, 14 Oct) and the stock rose about 18% from 8 Oct into the print alongside every London REIT. What is new is the 30 Sep valuation, NTA, EPRA EPS, dividend and rental-growth guide. Peers that have already reported (British Land campuses +1.6% values / +3.9% ERV, Landsec offices +0.4% / +3.4% ERV) and GPE's own 'in line with September 2026' sale price point to a modest NTA rise with the 4-7% rental guide on track. That supports a small positive sum (+0.35) and a near-coin-flip p_up of 53 on a ~3% move. The gap between the two numbers is the sector run-up plus a reiterated guide, both of which pull p_up toward 50.

already_public.what: H1 leasing: 40 leases and renewals, GBP19.0m annual rent, 4.1% ahead of March 2026 ERV (Q2 5.0%); GBP9.8m under offer 6.7% ahead of ERV; 30 Duke Street completed on time and budget, fully pre-let; Moody's Baa2 maintained; interim results date set for 19 Nov 2026
Sale of 2 Aldermanbury Square to Rothesay, net GBP368.7m, NIY 5.25%, about 3% ahead of March 2026 book and in line with September 2026 book; proceeds repay the RCF and fund the pipeline
Commitment to redevelop Soho Square Estate, W1 (c.90,000 sq ft, completion summer 2030)
FY27 guidance: rental value growth 4.0%-7.0% (prime offices 4.0%-8.0%); 10%+ ROE target for FY27; March 2026 EPRA NTA 524p; FY26 EPRA EPS 8.5p; FY26 total dividend 8.2p

new_in_release.expect: 30 Sep 2026 valuation and EPRA NTA: modestly up versus 524p (roughly +1-3%), on peer ERV growth of about 3-4% over six months, small yield expansion, and a development uplift from completing 30 Duke Street; direction positive, size uncertain
FY27 rental value growth guide of 4-7% most likely reiterated. Peers report H1 ERV of +3.0% to +3.9%, so it is on track; a raise to the upper end is possible but unsourced
H1 EPRA EPS: higher on Fully Managed NOI and 30 Duke Street income, offset by capitalised interest falling as schemes complete; no sourced bar
interim dividend: unknown; last year 2.9p, held flat
LTV pro forma for the Aldermanbury sale falls; capex to come rises with the Soho Square commitment; neutral
capital recycling: further sales under consideration (GBP200m flagged in May). A buyback is unlikely because the company said the proceeds go to the RCF and the pipeline

bar: No sourced H1 consensus for NTA or EPS. At FY26 the company published a compiled consensus (NTA 523p, EPS 7.9p; Visible Alpha NTA 522p) in its own RNS footnote (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/great-portland-estates--gpe/executing-our-growth-strategy/9578812), but none exists before this release. The bar is therefore unsourced; the reference points are March NTA of 524p and the 4-7% FY27 rental guide. Every finding is capped small.

findings.finding: Peers that reported for the same six months to 30 Sep 2026 show positive London office ERV and values. British Land campuses: values +1.6%, ERV +3.9%, yields +6bp, FY27 EPS guide upgraded. Landsec office-led: ERV +3.4% 'tracking ahead of guidance', office values +0.4%. Read across, GPE's ERV is on track inside its 4-7% FY guide and its H1 NTA is modestly up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HY interims 18 Nov 2025 (valuation +1.5%, NTA +2.0%, rental guide reiterated): stock -2.0%. FY26 results 21 May 2026 (NTA +6.1%, beat company consensus 523p): +1.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The sector re-rated about 13-18% since 8 Oct (GPE 300.8p to 354.8p, BLND 384.8p to 436.2p, LAND 601p to 698.5p per Yahoo daily closes), and peers moved only about +1% on their own results days (LAND +0.86% on 13 Nov, BLND +0.97% intraday on 18 Nov). That is what a priced read-across looks like. The residual is GPE's heavier West End and development tilt (30 Duke Street completion, 37% projected profit on cost), which peer portfolio averages understate.

findings.finding: GPE sold 2 Aldermanbury Square (about 12% of a GBP3.0bn portfolio) at a net GBP368.7m, which the company says is about 3% ahead of March 2026 book and 'in line with September 2026'. So the 30 Sep valuer marked that City HQ up about 3% in H1, and a transaction now validates that mark.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior disposals above book (Newman Street, Oct 2025) did not stop a -2.0% interims-day reaction; the day of this sale announcement, 16 Nov 2026, the stock rose 1.24%.
findings.original_quote: The net sale price is around 3% ahead of March 2026 book value and in line with September 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was public three sessions before the print, and the stock rose 1.24% on 16 Nov then gave it back (-1.89% on 17 Nov). The residual is that it is the one hard data point on the 30 Sep book, and it confirms rather than surprises.

findings.finding: H1 leasing slowed against last year: GBP19.0m at 4.1% over ERV, against GBP37.6m at 7.1% over ERV in H1 FY26 and 10.3% over ERV in FY26. The pricing premium narrowed, although Q2 (5.0%) improved on Q1 (3.7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 update carrying these numbers on 14 Oct 2026 moved the stock +2.96% (the sector also rallied that day: BLND +2.15%, LAND +2.67%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: pre-released on 14 Oct and absorbed with a positive reaction, so it is worth 0 unless the release revises it. Filed because it is the reason the rental guide is more likely reiterated than raised.
findings.independence: Prior-year H1 comparison from the issuer's own Nov 2025 interims: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/great-portland-estates--gpe/delivering-our-growth-strategy/9239859

findings.finding: Two large long holders trimmed into the print: BlackRock from 14.35% to 13.81% (3 Nov), and Janus Henderson below 5% (4.96%, 27 Oct, part of it in cash-settled CFDs).
findings.why_not_priced: Small and public. The stock still rose about 1% between the filings and the seal, so the selling was absorbed. Passive and index rebalancing cannot be distinguished from a view.

baseline_tension: The small positive findings run against the -0.46 lean (the 20-day run-up of +9.3%) and agree with the sector re-rating. The run-up means the peer read is largely in the price, which is why p_up sits at 53 rather than higher.

Peer read-across went from +0.4 to +0.3 (a narrow proxy, partly priced by the sector run-up)

'You were right about the number and too small about the move': abs_move_pct went from 2.8 to 3.0. The valuation, NTA, EPS and dividend are new even though leasing is pre-released, and the guide is most likely reiterated (measured median 2.3-3.1%)
